task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: largest gainer in absent player's primary types
minutes / initiations / same-position minutes as alternative predictors
methodological_questions: Does the teammate most similar in pre-absence initiation profile gain most in the absent player's primary play types?
Do minutes, initiations or same-position minutes predict the largest gainer better than similarity?
What is the unit of analysis (spell vs case) given n=148 spells but only 11 cases?
How to avoid mechanical floor, regression to the mean and label error when identifying gainers?

historical_evidence.finding: Exploratory map of about 23 absences. Mean replacement similarity was +0.863 for ABSORBED vs +0.848 for CASCADE. Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19, wrong-signed. Embiid 23-24 cascaded with Reed at similarity 0.94. Recorded failure evidence: similarity does not separate absorption from cascade and is almost always findable. Labeled non-confirmatory; sample and power NOT_RECORDED; no validation recorded; automated single-record adjudication (confidence 0.8) with failure mechanism B_powered_null and risk LABEL_ERROR.
Within-game adaptation study, a different question. Its record is limited by selection or regression to the mean, and its no-signal baseline was the highest dPPP.
Within-scheme re-test controlling early-PPP selection, a different question. Mechanism unclear from [prior work].
Travel x fit screen on post-move outcomes, n=198 movers. Fit-score correlations were negative and thresholds were in-sample. It concerns movers rather than absences, so it is only loosely related.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using replacement similarity of the best-matching teammate to separate absorption from cascade, tested by mean similarity and Spearman correlation.
failed_approaches.why: Similarity does not separate absorption from cascade and is almost always findable. The correlation was wrong-signed, and the study was exploratory with no recorded sample size or power.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive comparison of adapters with non-adapters without handling selection.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as limited by selection or regression to the mean; status artifact.

evidence_establishes: In one exploratory, non-confirmatory look at about 23 absences ([prior work][prior work]), similarity of the best replacement did not predict absorption versus cascade, and the sign was opposite to the hypothesis.
High-similarity teammates are almost always available, so similarity has little discriminating variance as a predictor.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types. [prior work][prior work] tested absorb vs cascade, not the identity of the top gainer.
Whether minutes, initiations or same-position minutes predict the top gainer. No retrieved record addresses these.
Whether the [prior work][prior work] null is robust. Its sample size and power are not recorded, and it carries only an inconclusive status with automated adjudication.
Anything about the 2025-26 data or the full 148 spells.
own_inferences: The stated 11 cases against 148 spells suggests spells cluster in few absent players. Spells of the same player are not independent, so the effective sample size is closer to 11 than to 148 for between-player claims.

Under a null with about 4-8 rotation teammates, the chance that any one pre-specified predictor picks the top gainer is about 1/k. Minutes and initiations are collinear with usage opportunity, so they will beat chance mainly through mechanical exposure.

The question bundles four predictors (closest profile, most minutes, most initiations, most same-position minutes). Without a pre-specified primary predictor, any positive finding is vulnerable to multiple testing.

If gainer is defined as the largest raw increase in the absent player's primary types, high-volume teammates have a mechanical advantage, since they have the most room to add absolute volume. Share-based or rate-based definitions would reverse some of that.
The likely result is a weak or null similarity effect, with volume-based predictors doing somewhat better than chance, possibly for mechanical reasons.
uncertainties: Definitions of spell, case and primary types are not given, and neither is the threshold for a gainer.
It is unknown whether the 148 spells and 11 cases overlap the roughly 23 absences in [prior work][prior work].
Lineup composition, opponent and garbage-time changes during absences are not described.
The similarity metric used in [prior work][prior work] is not recorded, so comparability is unclear.
Whether an absence-free baseline per teammate exists for estimating regression to the mean is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have rated the similarity hypothesis as plausible. [prior work][prior work] recorded a wrong-signed, near-null association with similarity, and similarity is almost always available. That lowered the predicted support for the similarity version and moved the decision to proceed_with_changes: a pre-registered, single-primary-predictor test with cluster-aware inference and a comparison against volume baselines. [prior work]'s inconclusive status, exploratory label and unrecorded power mean it does not close the question.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases. Between-player inference has low power, and 148 spells are clustered within those cases.
Minutes, initiations and same-position minutes are collinear with similarity and with opportunity. Their separate effects cannot be isolated with 11 cases.
Four candidate predictors with no designated primary one.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] is an exploratory, non-confirmatory look at about 23 absences, with a wrong-signed null for similarity against absorb/cascade. It is related but not identical, because it concerns the absorb-or-cascade label and not the top-gainer identity. It offers no evidence on minutes, initiations or same-position minutes.

risks.text: Effective n is near 11 cases. Top-gainer hit rates against a 1/k chance baseline are poorly estimated.
High-volume teammates can show the largest absolute gains simply because they have the most volume and the highest exposure. Volume predictors are favoured under raw-gain definitions.
Teammates with low pre-absence frequency in the primary types can gain by regression to the mean. Absences may also be selected around slumps or injuries.
Absence coincides with other lineup changes, opponent strength, back-to-backs, trades and coaching changes. Absent players with different primary types have different replacement structures.
Initiation profiles from short pre-absence windows are noisy. Per-teammate gains in sparse play types are noisy.
Few possessions in the absent player's primary types during short spells.
The gainer label depends on play-type classification and on the definition of primary types. [prior work][prior work] carries a LABEL_ERROR risk.
Four predictors and possible multiple definitions of gainer and primary types.
If the similarity profile or primary types are computed using data that overlaps the absence window, the predictor is contaminated.
Play-type frequencies and roles drift within and across seasons, so pre-absence baselines may be stale.

design.estimand: For each absence spell, whether the teammate with the highest pre-absence initiation-profile similarity to the absent player (the primary predictor) is the teammate with the largest absence-induced gain in the absent player's primary play types. Gain is the change in that teammate's share of team possessions in those types, with absence minus presence measured against the teammate's own presence baseline. The estimand is the top-1 hit rate against a spell-specific chance baseline (1/k, or the permutation expectation), plus the rank correlation of similarity with gain. Minutes, initiations and same-position minutes are secondary, pre-specified comparators, not co-primary.
design.unit: Absence spell, nested within the absent-player case (n=148 spells, 11 cases). Inference is at the case level, or spells weighted so that each case contributes equally.
design.sample: All spells in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs that meet pre-registered criteria. These should include a minimum number of absent-player primary-type possessions in the spell, a minimum teammate pre-absence minutes, and at least 4 eligible teammates. Pre-absence profiles use only games before the spell, with a fixed window. Exclusions (garbage time, ejections, trades) are fixed before looking at outcomes. Report the 11 cases and spell counts per case, and flag any overlap with [prior work][prior work].
design.power: With 11 cases, the minimum detectable effect is large. Before the test, simulate the permutation null using the actual k per spell and the within-case clustering, and report the minimum detectable hit-rate lift. If the minimum detectable lift exceeds a plausible effect (for example, more than about 15-20 percentage points over chance), label the result as underpowered and exploratory and do not claim a null.
design.controls: Use share- or rate-based gains normalised by each teammate's baseline, not raw volume, to limit the mechanical floor. Handle RTM by a placebo using matched pseudo-absence games with the absent player present, and by a baseline estimated on games well before the spell. Compare against the volume predictors with the same gain definition. Compute similarity only from pre-spell data. Adjust or stratify for opponent strength, back-to-backs, and spell length. Use a fixed minimum-possession threshold for the gain.
design.falsification: The similarity hypothesis is rejected if the case-level hit rate is not above permutation chance, or if the Spearman correlation between similarity and gain is not positive. This matches the wrong-signed result in [prior work][prior work]. A placebo using pseudo-spells with the player present should give hit rates at chance. If the placebo shows similar hit rates, the effect is declared an artifact. Also check a negative control with randomly shuffled similarity assigned within spell.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (similarity top-1 hit rate). The three volume predictors are secondary, with Holm correction across the four predictor tests. Definitions of gainer, primary types and thresholds are fixed beforehand with no post-hoc alternative definitions; any sensitivity analyses are labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Support the claim only if the case-clustered lower confidence bound for the similarity hit-rate lift over the permutation baseline is above zero, the placebo is at chance, and the result survives the share-based gain definition. Declare a null only if the minimum detectable lift is below the pre-registered plausible effect size and the confidence interval excludes it. Otherwise report inconclusive. Compare similarity to the volume predictors only descriptively unless the Holm-adjusted differences are significant.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type possession records for the 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs and the complete 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-01. Freeze the extraction date, the play-type derivation code version, the spell list and the case list before analysis.
